versions.short: The law sets clearer rules for deciding which country's social security system applies to EU workers who live or work in another EU member state, covering workers posted abroad, people working in more than one country, and cross-border workers. It keeps unemployed people's benefits for up to six months after they leave a country's employment services and clarifies which country pays unemployment benefits to cross-border workers. It also sets a clearer legal framework for sickness, long-term care and family benefits, including the right to necessary care during a stay abroad, and it encourages countries to share information quickly to catch errors and fraud, and requires that applications for the rules be possible fully online.
